title: Staggered cutover proxy with KV sync and adaptive backpressure
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: implement an edge-side, staged cutover proxy that enables active-active failover for the hosted API gateway while preserving streaming session continuity and meeting p99/p95 latency and availability SLOs.

Background: we operate multi-region edges that must be able to fail over traffic without long stalls or user-visible stream resets. Current abrupt region drains cause reconnect storms and token replays for long-lived streaming sessions. We need a solution that: (1) allows traffic to be shifted gradually between regions for capacity events, (2) preserves session KV/prefix cache state to avoid expensive cold starts, (3) applies backpressure and load-shedding early at the edge, and (4) integrates with existing circuit-breaker policies and service routing (smart routing/fallback).

High-level approach: create a lightweight proxy component (edge cutover proxy) co-located with the existing gateway that can: (A) orchestrate staggered traffic cutovers via traffic slices (10%, 30%, 60%, 100%) and coordinate with origin region to pre-warm session state, (B) perform async cross-region KV sync for session prefix/KV cache using sequence numbers and tombstones (no sync-on-write across regions), (C) implement adaptive backpressure at the connection level using measured in-flight token counts and CPU/queue thresholds, (D) expose local circuit-breaker signals that tie into global routing decisions, and (E) provide streaming resume semantics via a small resume handshake protocol (resume-token + last-ack seq) to rehydrate prefix cache on new region when required.

Design trade-offs considered: synchronous replication would provide stronger consistency but would add cross-region write latency and hurt SLOs. We choose eventual async KV replication supplemented by targeted rendezvous sync for heavy sessions during cutover windows. This keeps steady-state latency low while giving a path to fast recovery for high-cost sessions. There is an operational complexity trade-off: the proxy requires telemetry and runbooks to avoid split-brain routing during partial cutovers.

Deliverables: proxy implementation (go), cutover controller (control-plane changes), telemetry panels and alerts, end-to-end test harness (simulated multi-region traffic including streaming sessions), rollout automation (canaries and automated rollback).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Controlled cutover can shift traffic in staged slices (configurable: default 10/30/60/100) without manual intervention.
2) For controlled cutovers executed in staging, >= 99% of streaming sessions resume without application-level message loss (measured on test harness).
3) No degradation of p95 text-gen latency by more than 20% during normal staged cutovers; p99 must remain within SLO (see metrics).
4) Circuit-breaker signals are emitted and observed by global routing within 30s of breach and cause expected traffic routing change in canary runs.
5) Load-shedding triggers at edge when in-flight request queue > configured threshold and reduces new request acceptance rate; observable in metrics and reflected in synthetic traffic tests.
6) Telemetry: dashboards for cutover progress, per-slice session resume rate, KV-sync lag, and edge backpressure counters are shipping and documented.
7) Implementation has an accompanying runbook for emergency rollback and postmortem steps.
8) Security review completed for resume handshake and KV sync (KMS usage confirmed) before GA.

2025-02-14 - Design review (internal): Decided to prefer async KV replication with rendezvous sync for heavy sessions to avoid cross-region write latency during steady state. Action: add targeted sync API to control plane (ENG-22418 referenced).
2025-02-16 - SRE comment: Need clear backpressure thresholds per region; suggested starting defaults: queue-length 200, cpu > 75% triggers aggressive shedding. We'll refine with load tests.
2025-02-18 - Security review request submitted: https://security-review.internal/redwood/requests/EDGE-789; reviewer requested encryption of resume token in transit and at rest (KMS).

2025-02-19 - QA (J. Kim): E2E harness initial results: under simulated 20% region capacity drop, staged cutover prevented reconnect storms for 87% of streams. Need to tune rendezvous sync to get >95% before promoting to canary.

2025-02-20 - Marcus Liu: Implemented metrics export for kv_sync_lag_seconds and session_resume_success_rate. Pushed changes to PR and updated Confluence with dashboard links. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/1247
risks: Split-brain routing if control-plane and data-plane disagree on slice assignment during race windows.
KV-sync lag could lead to higher model token costs if sessions are rehydrated from origin repeatedly.
Complexity of resume protocol could introduce new attack surface if tokens are not properly encrypted/rotated.
If backpressure thresholds are tuned too aggressively, we may shed healthy traffic and violate SLAs for high-priority customers.
rollout_plan: 1) Unit + integration tests in CI for proxy and handshake.
2) Deploy proxy to staging region A and run E2E harness with synthetic streaming traffic (validate acceptance criteria).
3) Canary: enable 10% slice cutover between two regions for low-priority internal tenants for 24h; monitor session_resume_success_rate and kv_sync_lag_seconds.
4) Gradually increase slices (30% -> 60% -> 100%) with automated rollback if resume success < 95% or if p99 latency breaches SLO.
5) After successful canary across multiple regions, schedule GA with customer communication and updated SLA language.
metrics: SLO: availability >= 99.95% across hosted API endpoints (global) over 30d
Latency target: p95 < 180ms, p99 < 600ms for text generation during steady-state cutovers
edge_backpressure_rejections_per_minute (should be 0 in healthy steady-state; alert if > threshold)
circuit_breaker_open_events: alert if > baseline during cutover
